tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/OneParameterSemig.summary: Tau Ceti (TauCeti/Analysis/Semigroups, Normed/Operator/Resolvent, CompletelyMonotone, PositiveDefinite, Bochner) already contains essentially the whole roadmap on real Banach spaces: C₀ and contraction semigroups with generators, closedness, uniqueness, the real resolvent and its sharp power bounds, operator-norm analyticity of unbounded resolvents, bounded perturbation, both the Hille–Yosida and Lumer–Phillips theorems as iff statements, Hausdorff–Bernstein–Widder with uniqueness, Lévy–Khintchine, Bochner on finite-dimensional inner-product spaces and the Berg–Christensen–Ressel theorem; Mathlib contributes only AbsolutelyMonotoneOn, LinearPMap, charFun and Matrix.PosSemidef. Genuinely missing: uniqueness of solutions of the abstract Cauchy problem, a public statement of the integral formula for resolvent powers (it exists only as private lemmas), the half-plane complex resolvent set of the complexified generator, the reciprocal complete-Bernstein/Stieltjes correspondence, and the optional LCA Bochner stretch. The roadmap's Bernstein milestone, stated with C^∞ smoothness on [0,∞), is false in the converse direction; Tau Ceti proves the correct form with continuity at 0 and complete monotonicity on (0,∞). The milestone layers repeat text from their parent parts.

targets.target: C₀ semigroup structure and contraction-semigroup subclass
targets.note: Over a real Banach space: toFun : ℝ≥0 → X →L[ℝ] X with S 0 = id, S(s+t) = S s ∘ S t and strong continuity at 0; contraction semigroups extend it with ‖S t‖ ≤ 1.

targets.target: Growth bound ‖S t‖ ≤ M e^{ωt} and its existence
targets.note: HasGrowthBound ω M includes 1 ≤ M.

targets.target: Generator as strong derivative at 0 on its domain, as a LinearPMap
targets.note: The domain is the submodule of x for which (S t x − x)/t converges as t → 0⁺; the generator is a LinearPMap, as the roadmap requires.

targets.target: Density of D(A), and of D(Aⁿ)
targets.note: Both the named density theorem and the secondary D(Aⁿ) target are present.

targets.target: The generator determines the semigroup
The generator is closed
S(t)D(A) ⊆ D(A), A S(t)x = S(t)Ax, and differentiability of t ↦ S(t)x for x ∈ D(A)
targets.note: The orbit derivative is within [0,∞) at every t ≥ 0 and equals A S(t)x.

targets.target: Bounded generator (domain = ⊤) iff uniformly continuous semigroup
targets.note: Continuity is of t ↦ S t in operator norm; a semigroup with bounded generator A is exp(tA).

targets.target: Bounded perturbation theorem
targets.note: For bounded B, B + A generates a C₀ semigroup with growth bound (M, ω + M‖B‖).

targets.target: ∫₀ᵗ S(s)x ds ∈ D(A) with A∫₀ᵗ S(s)x ds = S(t)x − x
Dissipativity and m-dissipativity (Banach form); generator of a contraction semigroup is m-dissipative
targets.note: Dissipativity is the resolvent-range inequality λ‖x‖ ≤ ‖λx − Ax‖ for λ > 0, the general Banach notion the roadmap asks for.

targets.target: Hilbert characterization of dissipativity ⟪Ax, x⟫ ≤ 0
targets.note: Stated for real inner product spaces, as a specialization.

targets.target: Unbounded resolvent set and resolvent, with the bridge to Mathlib's resolvent for bounded operators
targets.note: λ ∈ ρ(A) iff λI − A : D(A) → X has a bounded two-sided inverse; defined over any nontrivially normed field.

targets.target: R(λ,A)x = ∫₀^∞ e^{−λt} S(t)x dt for real λ > ω
targets.note: The Laplace integral is a pointwise Bochner integral bundled into a continuous linear map, and is identified with the abstract resolvent of the generator.

targets.target: Resolvent identity R(λ) − R(μ) = (μ − λ)R(λ)R(μ)
Analyticity of λ ↦ R(λ,A) on the resolvent set
targets.note: Proved in operator norm for any unbounded operator on a Banach space over a nontrivially normed field, so both the real resolvent set of the generator and any complex resolvent set are covered. The 2026-09-03 STATUS.md lists this as missing; it is in the baseline.

targets.target: Complex resolvent set via complexification: Re λ > ω lies in the resolvent set of the complexified generator
targets.note: The complexified semigroup and complex generator exist, but no theorem places the half-plane Re λ > ω in the complex resolvent set or gives the Laplace formula for complex λ.

targets.target: Derivative formula dᵏR(λ,A)/dλᵏ = (−1)ᵏ k! R(λ,A)^{k+1}
targets.note: Stated for the real resolvent function on λ > ω.

targets.target: Power formula R(λ,A)ⁿx = ∫₀^∞ tⁿ⁻¹/(n−1)! e^{−λt} S(t)x dt
targets.note: Both halves are proved, but only as private declarations in PowerBounds.lean (the moment integral and its identification with the resolvent power); there is no public statement of the integral formula.

targets.target: Iterated resolvent bounds ‖R(λ,A)ⁿ‖ ≤ M/(λ−ω)ⁿ; contraction corollary ‖R(λ,A)‖ ≤ 1/λ
Hille–Yosida generation theorem at general (M, ω)
targets.note: Real Banach space X; densely defined A with (ω,∞) in its resolvent set and ‖R(λ,A)ⁿ‖ ≤ M/(λ−ω)ⁿ for n ≥ 1 generates a C₀ semigroup with growth bound (M, ω). The iff version also proves necessity.

targets.target: Yosida approximation A_λ = λ²R(λ,A) − λI, contraction exponentials, compact-time Cauchy limit and generator identification
targets.note: The limit semigroup is defined from the uniformly Cauchy exponentials (not as a limit to a pre-existing S), and its generator is identified with A; the Hille–Yosida route uses the analogous hilleYosidaLimitSemigroup.

targets.target: Lumer–Phillips generation theorem (dissipative + range condition gives contraction semigroup)
targets.note: IsMDissipative is exactly dissipativity plus surjectivity of λ₀ − A for some λ₀ > 0, as in the roadmap; density of the domain is a separate hypothesis, and the iff adds the converse.

targets.target: Abstract Cauchy problem: t ↦ S(t)x is a classical solution for x ∈ D(A)
targets.note: IsClassicalSolution requires u(0) = x, u(t) ∈ D(A), and a continuous right derivative on [0,∞) equal to A u(t).

targets.target: Abstract Cauchy problem: t ↦ S(t)x is a mild solution for every x
targets.note: IsMildSolution: continuity on [0,∞), u(0) = x, and ∫₀ᵗ u ∈ D(A) with A∫₀ᵗ u = u(t) − x.

targets.target: Uniqueness: every classical (or mild) solution of u' = Au, u(0) = x equals S(t)x
targets.note: Only the interpolation lemma behind generator uniqueness exists; no theorem states that a classical or mild solution of the abstract Cauchy problem must be the semigroup orbit, so 'the solution' is proved as existence only.

targets.target: Acceptance examples: multiplication semigroup with generator −m, e^{tA} for bounded A, Neumann-series resolvent, resolvent identity and ‖R(λ)‖ ≤ 1/λ
targets.note: The multiplication semigroup is on bounded continuous functions α →ᵇ ℝ with a bounded continuous multiplier m, so its generator is bounded; the resolvent identity and the 1/λ bound are proved for all semigroups and contraction semigroups respectively.

duplicates.note: PDE Lane F item 26 asks for generators and the Hille–Yosida theorem (with the heat semigroup), which this part states in full generality.
The parent Lane F restates item 26's generators and Hille–Yosida.

targets.target: Hille–Yosida generation theorem at general (M, ω)
targets.note: Real Banach space X; densely defined A with (ω,∞) in its resolvent set and ‖R(λ,A)ⁿ‖ ≤ M/(λ−ω)ⁿ for n ≥ 1 generates a C₀ semigroup with growth bound (M, ω). The iff version also proves necessity.

targets.target: Sharp power bounds on the resolvent of a generator (the necessity half)
targets.note: Not required by the milestone statement itself, but proved and packaged in hilleYosida_generation_iff.

duplicates.note: PDE Lane F item 26 lists the Hille–Yosida theorem among its semigroup targets.
The parent Lane F restates item 26's Hille–Yosida target.

targets.target: Density sub-lemma and stability estimates for the Yosida exponentials
targets.note: λR(λ,A)x → x and A_λx → Ax on D(A) give the approximation estimates; density of the generator domain is proved for every C₀ semigroup.

targets.target: Abstract Cauchy problem: t ↦ S(t)x is a classical solution for x ∈ D(A)
targets.note: IsClassicalSolution requires u(0) = x, u(t) ∈ D(A), and a continuous right derivative on [0,∞) equal to A u(t).

targets.note: IsMildSolution: continuity on [0,∞), u(0) = x, and ∫₀ᵗ u ∈ D(A) with A∫₀ᵗ u = u(t) − x.

targets.target: Uniqueness: every classical (or mild) solution of u' = Au, u(0) = x equals S(t)x
targets.note: Only the interpolation lemma behind generator uniqueness exists; no theorem states that a classical or mild solution of the abstract Cauchy problem must be the semigroup orbit, so 'the solution' is proved as existence only.

targets.target: The displayed Lean stubs hilleYosida_generation and lumerPhillips
targets.note: The stubs printed under this milestone restate the two generation theorems, which are proved with the same hypotheses (no DenseLinearOperator wrapper is needed: density is a hypothesis on a LinearPMap).

targets.target: Acceptance examples: multiplication semigroup with generator −m, e^{tA} for bounded A, Neumann-series resolvent, resolvent identity and ‖R(λ)‖ ≤ 1/λ
targets.note: The multiplication semigroup is on bounded continuous functions α →ᵇ ℝ with a bounded continuous multiplier m, so its generator is bounded; the resolvent identity and the 1/λ bound are proved for all semigroups and contraction semigroups respectively.

targets.target: IsCompletelyMonotone with bundled C^∞ smoothness on [0,∞)
targets.note: Defined exactly as ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ f (Ici 0) with alternating signs of iteratedDerivWithin; open-half-line and continuous-at-0 variants, and a set-based version built on Mathlib's AbsolutelyMonotoneOn, are also provided.

targets.target: Bernstein functions
targets.note: Continuous and nonnegative on [0,∞), smooth on (0,∞), with completely monotone derivative on (0,∞).

targets.target: Closure under sums and nonnegative scalar multiples
Closure under products
Closure under pointwise limits
targets.note: Stated on the open half-line (plus continuity at 0 for the closed version), which is the form in which the class is closed: smoothness at 0 is not preserved by pointwise limits.

targets.target: Composition g ∘ f of completely monotone g with Bernstein f
targets.note: The open-half-line version needs f > 0 on (0,∞); the continuous version has no extra hypothesis.

targets.target: Derivative and integral closure
targets.note: −f' is completely monotone; the primitive of a completely monotone function is Bernstein.

targets.target: Extreme rays t ↦ e^{−tx} and their mixtures
Completely monotone ↔ Bernstein correspondences
targets.note: f is Bernstein iff f ≥ 0 and e^{−xf} is completely monotone for all x > 0; derivatives and primitives move between the two classes.

targets.target: Stieltjes and complete Bernstein function relationships
targets.note: Stieltjes functions are exactly constants plus Laplace transforms of completely monotone functions, and f is Stieltjes iff t·f(t) is complete Bernstein (both iff, contrary to the older STATUS.md). Missing: the reciprocal correspondence, a nonzero f is complete Bernstein iff 1/f is Stieltjes.

targets.target: Lévy–Khintchine representation of Bernstein functions, with uniqueness of the triplet
targets.note: f = a + bt + ∫(1 − e^{−tx}) μ(dx) on [0,∞) with ∫ min(1,x) dμ < ∞.

targets.target: Bernstein (Hausdorff–Bernstein–Widder) theorem: complete monotonicity on [0,∞) iff Laplace transform of a unique finite measure on ℝ≥0
targets.note: Proved with the correct closed-half-line hypothesis IsContinuousCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi (continuous on [0,∞), completely monotone on (0,∞)). The roadmap's literal statement with IsCompletelyMonotone (C^∞ on [0,∞)) is false in the converse direction: a finite measure without a finite first moment has a Laplace transform that is not differentiable at 0. Tau Ceti also proves the forward direction from the smooth predicate and the converse under finite moments.

targets.target: Open half-line version: complete monotonicity on (0,∞) iff Laplace transform of a unique, possibly infinite, measure; 1/t example
Uniqueness via Laplace-transform injectivity
targets.note: Finite measures on ℝ≥0 are determined by their Laplace transform at the natural numbers.

targets.target: Measure extraction via Prokhorov tightness
targets.note: Existence goes through tight rescaled Chafaï approximating measures and a weak cluster point.

targets.target: Acceptance examples: e^{−t} ↦ δ₁, 1/(1+t) ↦ e^{−x}dx, closure used to build new examples
Bernstein (Hausdorff–Bernstein–Widder) theorem: complete monotonicity on [0,∞) iff Laplace transform of a unique finite measure on ℝ≥0
targets.note: Proved with the correct closed-half-line hypothesis IsContinuousCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi (continuous on [0,∞), completely monotone on (0,∞)). targets.target: Acceptance examples: e^{−t} ↦ δ₁, 1/(1+t) ↦ e^{−x}dx, closure used to build new examples
IsPositiveDefinite on an involutive additive monoid (involution form Σ cᵢ c̄ⱼ F(aᵢ + aⱼ⋆) ≥ 0)
targets.note: Defined on [AddMonoid M] [StarAddMonoid M], slightly more general than the roadmap's AddCommMonoid.

targets.target: Instances: V with a⋆ = −a, and the BCR involution (t, a)⋆ = (t, −a) on ℝ≥0 × V
targets.note: IsSemigroupGroupPD is IsPositiveDefinite on a private carrier with the BCR involution rather than on the product StarAddMonoid instance; the notion is the same.

targets.target: Closure under sums, scalar multiples, products and Schur products
Conjugate symmetry, (F 0).im = 0, 0 ≤ (F 0).re and ‖F a‖ ≤ (F 0).re
targets.note: The norm bound needs a⋆ = −a (or a + a⋆ = 0), which is when it holds.

targets.target: Continuity at 0 implies uniform continuity
targets.note: For the group involution a⋆ = −a.

targets.target: Pointwise limits preserve positive-definiteness; locally uniform limits preserve continuity
targets.note: Continuity of a locally uniform limit is Mathlib's generic TendstoLocallyUniformly.continuous; the roadmap's warning that pointwise limits need not be continuous is respected.

targets.target: PD-function ↔ PD-kernel equivalence, pullbacks, normalization F(0) = 1
targets.note: Kernels are expressed through Matrix.PosSemidef on arbitrary index types.

targets.target: GNS/Kolmogorov decomposition of a positive-definite kernel
Fourier-convention conversion lemma (e^{−2πi⟨·,·⟩} vs characteristic function)
Bridge lemma: the Fourier transform of a finite measure is continuous positive definite
Bochner's theorem on a finite-dimensional real inner-product space V (iff, unique finite measure), with ℝᵈ corollary
targets.note: Continuous and positive definite (group form F(a − b), equivalent to the involution form with a⋆ = −a) iff F(v) = ∫ e^{−2πi⟨v,q⟩} dμ for a unique finite Borel μ (fourierAtom is not in declarations.tsv because its line starts with `public`). The optional LCA/Pontryagin stretch is absent (Mathlib has PontryaginDual but no Bochner theorem).

targets.target: Berg–Christensen–Ressel theorem on ℝ≥0 × V: bounded continuous positive-definite functions are Laplace–Fourier transforms of unique finite measures
targets.note: Stated as an iff, with existence consuming Bochner through spatial slices and uniqueness by Laplace–Fourier injectivity.

targets.target: Acceptance examples: Bochner on V = ℝ, V = 0 collapse of BCR to Bernstein, Gaussian e^{−‖a‖²} positive definite with Gaussian representing measure
targets.note: V = ℝ and V = 0 are instances of the general theorems, and the Gaussian's representing measure is determined by its characteristic function; the identifications are not recorded as separate named statements.
